questions.text: What is COBIT 2019 mainly used for?

options.A: Governance and management of enterprise IT
options.B: Certifying an information security management system
options.C: Running day-to-day IT service desk operations

questions.explanation: COBIT is ISACA's framework for governance and management of enterprise IT (ISO 27001 = ISMS; COSO = internal control; ITIL = service management).

questions.text: Which of these is NOT a component of the COSO 2013 internal control framework?
questions.explanation: The five components are control environment, risk assessment, control activities, information and communication, and monitoring activities.

questions.text: Which of these is a detective control?

options.A: Input checks that reject invalid dates as data is keyed
options.B: A system rule requiring two approvals before payment release
options.C: Password rules requiring length and complexity at login
options.D: Reviewing an exception report of posted manual journals

questions.explanation: Reviewing entries after posting finds problems that already happened; the other options stop them from happening (preventive).

questions.text: An auditor finds that developers have write access to the production database. What is the main risk?

options.A: Data can be changed outside change and application controls
options.B: The production database may run out of disk storage space quickly
options.C: Developers may take longer to finish their projects
options.D: Overnight backups may take longer than scheduled

questions.explanation: Direct write access lets data be altered without approval, testing or audit trail through the normal application.

questions.text: What is the main purpose of the planning phase of an internal audit?

options.A: Agree action plans and target dates for each finding
options.B: Set the objectives, scope and risk-based approach
options.C: Write the final report and agree it with management
options.D: Test every transaction in the period under review

questions.explanation: Planning sets objectives and scope and focuses work on the key risks before fieldwork starts.

questions.text: What is a key advantage of statistical sampling over judgmental sampling?

options.A: Sampling risk can be measured and results projected
options.B: It always needs a smaller sample than other methods
options.C: It removes the need for any auditor judgement
options.D: It focuses the sample on the highest-value items

questions.explanation: Statistical sampling quantifies sampling risk and supports projecting results; it doesn't always mean smaller samples or no judgement.

questions.text: A finding states: "30% of changes to vendor bank details had no supporting request form." Which element of the finding is this?
questions.explanation: It describes what the auditor actually found, which is the condition.

questions.text: In an audit finding, what does the "effect" describe?

options.A: The facts the auditor observed during testing
options.B: The underlying reason the problem occurred
options.C: The actual or potential impact on the organisation
options.D: The standard or policy that should have been met

questions.explanation: The effect explains why the finding matters, e.g. the potential loss or misstatement.

questions.text: What does the recovery time objective (RTO) define?

options.A: How long backup copies are retained for
options.B: The maximum acceptable time to restore a system
options.C: How often backups of the system are taken
options.D: The maximum acceptable amount of data that can be lost

questions.explanation: RTO is the target time to restore service; RPO is about data loss.

questions.text: A company backs up its critical systems every night but has never tried restoring from those backups. What should the auditor recommend?

options.A: Move backups to a different storage vendor
options.B: Keep each backup for a longer retention period
options.C: Take backups twice a day instead of once
options.D: Test restores periodically to prove backups work

questions.explanation: A backup that has never been restored gives no assurance it works; periodic restore testing provides that assurance.

questions.text: What does the principle of least privilege mean?

options.A: Only managers are allowed any system access
options.C: All access is reviewed at least once a year
options.D: Users get only the access their job requires

questions.explanation: Least privilege limits each user to the minimum access their role needs.

questions.text: How many controls are listed in Annex A of ISO/IEC 27001:2022?
questions.explanation: The 2022 edition has 93 Annex A controls in four themes; the 2013 edition had 114.

questions.text: During fieldwork, the auditee refuses to provide system logs, saying they are confidential. What is the best next step?

options.A: Skip the test quietly and leave it out of the report
options.B: Conclude the control is effective since no issue was found
options.C: Obtain the logs from another system administrator without consent
options.D: Escalate under the audit charter and record the scope limitation

questions.explanation: The audit charter gives access rights; a refusal is a scope limitation to escalate and document, not bypass or ignore.

questions.text: To keep it independent, the head of internal audit should report functionally to:

options.C: The audit committee of the board

questions.explanation: Functional reporting to the board or audit committee protects independence; administrative reporting is often to the CEO.

questions.text: Which behaviour is a common red flag for fraud?

options.A: Documents their work carefully and keeps records tidy
options.B: Never takes leave and won't let others do their tasks
options.C: Regularly asks for extra training and development
options.D: Takes all of their annual leave entitlement every year

questions.explanation: Avoiding leave and refusing to share tasks can hide ongoing concealment, which is why mandatory leave is a fraud control.

questions.text: In the IIA Three Lines Model, which is an example of a second-line role?

options.B: A sales team applying pricing controls
options.D: A risk management or compliance function

questions.explanation: The second line provides expertise, monitoring and challenge on risk (e.g. risk, compliance); the first line is operational management.

questions.text: Sales data is transferred daily from the order system to the general ledger, but nobody reconciles the records sent with the records received. What is the main risk?

options.A: Missing or duplicated records go undetected
options.B: The order system slows down at month end
options.C: Users forget their passwords for the ledger
options.D: The ledger needs more storage each year

questions.explanation: Without an interface reconciliation, dropped or duplicated records can reach the financial statements unnoticed.

questions.text: What is the main purpose of a walkthrough?

options.A: Test that a control operated correctly across the whole year
options.B: Agree the final report wording with management
options.C: Confirm understanding of the process and key controls
options.D: Count physical inventory at the period end

questions.explanation: A walkthrough follows a transaction end to end to confirm understanding and control design before testing.

questions.text: What does testing the operating effectiveness of a control determine?

options.A: Whether management finds it useful and practical
options.B: Whether it worked consistently throughout the period
options.C: Whether it is written down in a procedure document
options.D: Whether it is designed to address the relevant risk

questions.explanation: Design testing asks "could it work?"; operating effectiveness asks "did it work consistently over the period?".

questions.text: An auditor wants to test whether all goods shipped were invoiced (completeness). Which direction of testing is correct?

options.A: Trace shipping documents forward to invoices
options.B: Recalculate the totals on a sample of invoices
options.C: Send confirmations to a sample of customers
options.D: Trace invoices back to shipping documents

questions.explanation: Completeness is tested from the source (shipments) forward to the record (invoices); tracing invoices back tests occurrence instead.
